title: Falkirk Digital — ops + on‑prem inference call digest
content:
Call snapshot (2025-11-04) — attendees: Tom Reed (Falkirk Digital, Head of Platform), Priya Shah (security), Maya T. (Redwood SE), Ethan P. (Redwood infra lead)

High-level ask:
- Falkirk wants a private, VPC-hosted Redwood stack (no public egress) to serve a document-summarization feature embedded in their product. Must support peak of ~450 qps (small prompts + long context caching) with 99th pct latency <120ms per token. Target rollout in Q1 2026 (pilot mid-Jan).

Constraints / must-haves noted by customer:
- No external model hosting; all model artifacts must live inside their VPC or on-prem storage behind their KMS.
- SOC2 + ISO27001 compliance required for pilot. They will supply an IP allowlist and want mTLS for all service-to-service comms.
- KMS/HSM integration: prefer AWS KMS with a dedicated key, but have HSM appliance on-prem for secrets in air-gapped sites.
- Network: strict egress policy, private subnets only. Need guidance on NAT vs. VPC endpoints.
- GPU preference: they mentioned interest in NVidia L40s or equivalent; cost/availability unknown.
- Data residency: EU region for EU users, US for NA. Want same control plane but per-region private control plane instances (we discussed tradeoffs).

Technical gotchas / red flags (from call):
- They use long-document workflows; naive KV cache sizing could blow memory on 8k+ contexts. Need explicit cache eviction policy and monitoring.
- Their client app expects near-immediate streaming; continuous batching may add jitter—must tune batching windows per route.
- Firewall rules: corporate infra team uses deep packet inspection; TLS termination proxies could break mTLS unless we recommend passthrough.
- Latency SLOs tight given token-per-ms requirements; quantization and kernel choice will matter.

Suggested architecture (quick sketch):
- Private Redwood control plane deployed in their VPC (small HA pair per region) talking to private serving clusters in same subnets.
- Serving nodes with pooled GPUs (suggest initial mix: 4x A30-equivalent for baseline, add 2x L40 if available for latency-critical routes).
- Put a per-customer edge proxy inside VPC to handle mTLS and route to model routes; no public ingress.
- Use Redis (inside VPC) for shared KV cache plus local in-memory per-worker LRU for prefixes.

Performance considerations / experiments to run during pilot:
- End-to-end latency matrix: cold vs warm cache, single-stream vs batched, 1‑token vs 32-token responses.
- Quantization experiment: int8 PPQ / GPTQ on 4k context model variant; evaluate latency vs quality regression on their eval set (10k prompt set).
- Batching policy: measure throughput/latency tradeoffs with 5ms, 10ms, 25ms windows.

Open questions (need follow-up):
- Exact expected prompt length distribution (they gave 3 samples; ask for histogram).
- Peak qps distribution by region/timezone (spiky or smooth?).
- Can they accept model fallbacks (smaller quantized variant) under heavy load? legal sign-off?
- Confirmation on whether their HSM requires gateway appliance for KMS calls (we need network diagrams).

Action items / owners:
- Maya: draft proposal + cost sketch for pilot (due 2025-11-08) -> include NVL/ A30 vs L40 cost scenarios.
- Ethan: validate runtime requirements with infra team (NV memory + kernel scheduling) and estimate GPU counts (due 2025-11-07).
- Tom / Priya (Falkirk): share prompt histograms and current compliance checklist (due 2025-11-10).
- Ravi: prepare short demo harness to show cache warmup and streaming behavior (P0 demo next week).

Possible risks & mitigations:
- Risk: mTLS breakage due to corporate TLS interception -> Mitigate: recommend TCP passthrough for worker communication; document handshake details for their security team.
- Risk: KMS integration latency (HSM gateway adds ms) -> Mitigate: local envelope keys + aggressive caching of DEKs in worker memory with rekeying policy.

Notes to self / follow-up items for Redwood docs:
- Add an example onprem KMS integration pattern (AWS KMS + on-prem HSM fallback).
- Create a sample firewall rule checklist for customers with DPI appliances.
- Capture batch tuning guidance in the Optimize playbook: include perf numbers for A30 vs L40 for 2k/4k contexts.

Meeting tone: pragmatic, security-focused, timeline-driven. They are motivated but risk-averse. Next checkin: 11/12 for proposal review.

Misc references: pilot budget they hinted ~ $30k/mo for initial capacity; if so we need conservative costing.

End of notes.
